summary: Round 2 re-review at 1af57a40. Of the seven round-1 findings, NAT-002 through NAT-007 are resolved in code, tests and NATIVE.md. NAT-001 is resolved for GPU semantics, but the fix introduces a new blocking defect, NAT-008, in the CPU path. DeliveryAccounting counts windows using Events._batch_event_count. That counter goes up for every envelope that has any dgram (events.py:99-101), and that includes transitions. The CPU path sends transitions through the Events stream: EventManager produces them from the SMD batch, mpi_ds._events_impl:547 swallows them via run._handle_transition, and steps() relies on BeginStep arriving there. The worker's `delivered` count, len(timestamps), counts only L1 events. So for CPU cases where a BD receives a transition (BeginStep is required for steps cases, and Enable/EndRun are normal), sum(windows)+drain > delivered and delivery.result() raises 'do not cover'. Four of the six raw cases would therefore fail closed at native execution. The NATIVE.md statement that window populations plus drain equal delivered events is also false for CPU. The GPU path is unaffected, because GpuEventManager._handle_steps dispatches transitions internally and only L1 envelopes are yielded. The offline stub does not model transitions, so this was not caught. Code acceptance is therefore not granted. Passing this code review in a later round would still not imply native qualification. All NATIVE.md qualification items remain outstanding: native API smoke; input/reference and private-copy preparation; isolated installs and provenance; compute-access and retention receipts; Slurm flag viability; real scheduler cancellation; instrumentation overhead; component bounds; then correctness and A/A.

findings.evidence: Resolved. The always-None manager lookup has been removed. accounting.finish() relies on the init hook. Provenance is recorded once before and once after, under distinct names (lines 217, 290).

DeliveryAccounting.end records events._batch_event_count. That counter goes up for every non-empty envelope, including transitions (events.py:99-101). On the CPU path, EventManager yields transitions from the SMD batch (event_manager.py:347-380, Enable handling at 209). These transitions reach the Run, which swallows them in _events_impl (mpi_ds.py:547 via run.py:617-624) and consumes BeginStep in steps() (mpi_ds.py:621-637). The worker passes delivered=len(timestamps) (line 282), which counts only L1 events yielded to the user. So for any CPU case whose BD receives a transition (BeginStep for the steps cases, and Enable/EndStep/EndRun in general), sum(yielded_events_per_delivery_window)+drain exceeds delivered. delivery.result() then raises 'delivery-window and drain populations do not cover delivered events', and the four CPU cases fail at native execution. first_nonempty_yield_window_seconds can also be set by a transition-only window. NATIVE.md:35-37 calls these 'yielded events' and says windows plus drain equal delivered events, which is untrue for CPU. The GPU path is not affected, because GpuEventManager._handle_steps dispatches transitions internally (gpu_events.py:797-840) and the CPU sub-loop drops non-L1 (gpu_events.py:1137). The offline stub test does not model transitions, so the defect is not exercised.
findings.requested_change: Count L1 events and transitions per window separately. One way is to wrap the per-window envelope stream, for example by wrapping events._evt_man or observing Events.__next__ return values and classifying with utils.first_service/TransitionId.isEvent. Require sum(L1 window counts)+L1 drain == len(timestamps), and record transition counts as their own field. Only set first_nonempty on the first window that contains L1 events. Update NATIVE.md and the assemble timing text to match. Add an offline stub test with transitions inside CPU windows, and in steps mode, showing that coverage holds and that a missing L1 event is still rejected.
